primitives.name: Factor Stripping Policy
primitives.verbatim_quote: Public response renders Free-tier projection of paid picks (Edge Index + grade visible, factor breakdown stripped).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'factor stripping policy {0: none, 1: partial, 2: full}', 'P': 'projection type {0: free, 1: pro}'}
primitives.assumptions: Public posts must strip Pro-tier factors for Free-tier viewers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: S = 2 when P = 1 and audience is Free-tier

layer2.mapping: Policy S(P, T) ensures factor integrity under visibility constraints; GSE enforces via state transition.
layer2.telemetry: Factor fields absent in public view for Free-tier users.

The core operator is tier-aware embed rendering, defined by a binary tier variable T ∈ {0,1} and a factor visibility function F(T). The ephemeral/public protocol K(R, T) governs response scope, where R ∈ {0,1} determines visibility. Factor stripping S(P, T) ensures that when P=1 (pro-tier pick) and T=0 (free-tier viewer), sensitive factor data is removed. These primitives form a layered access control system: (1) user tier is verified at runtime, (2) embeds are generated with conditional factor detail, (3) response mode selects visibility scope, and (4) public mode applies stripping policy. Failure modes include leaking paid content to free users (leakage), caching responses (anti-pattern), or posting teasers (non-compliance). The system enforces dualities: ephemeral ↔ public, free ↔ pro, and visible ↔ stripped. Mathematical consistency requires that each user’s response is computed independently and that no cached state persists across users.
